Hypersonic.title: Air Force Awards ARRW Production Contract, Adds Hypersonic Capability
points: The Department of the Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract for the production and fielding of the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, Sept. 29, 2026.

This milestone marks the formal transition of the boost-glide hypersonic missile program from prototyping and flight testing into production, solidifying the Air Force's commitment to fielding standoff, high-speed strike options.

Designed to accelerate to speeds exceeding Mach 5 using a solid-fuel rocket booster before releasing a hypersonic glide vehicle, ARRW will enable Air Force assets to strike time-sensitive, heavily defended and high-value targets from standoff ranges.

Hypersonic.title: AFRL Targets New Hypersonic Engine Tech Prototypes Within 4 Years
points: The Air Force Research Laboratory wants industry to advance concepts for affordable hypersonic munition engines to prototype demonstrations.
The notice is one of the first updates in months on its push for affordable rocket engines for hypersonic munitions.

The Hermes Rocket Lab effort began in 2020 under AFRL’s Rocket Propulsion Division with a Broad Agency Announcement seeking novel concepts and research and development proposals to accelerate rocket engine technology.

Hypersonic.title: UCF Researcher Designing Hypersonic Jet Engine for Seamless Atmospheric and Space Travel
points: The research aims to design a specialized dual-mode engine that may make hypersonic and space travel more efficient and accessible.
UCF Professor Kareem Ahmed is developing a dual-mode liquid detonation propulsion engine that will operate as an air-breathing engine at hypersonic speeds and transition into a rocket engine.
Continuing to advance the emerging field of hypersonic travel and build upon previous successes is something Ahmed is looking forward to with his dual-mode detonation engine research.

Air & Missile Defence.title: 9k-Mile 2011 Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor at No Reserve
points: This 2011 Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor spent time with one collector owner in Illinois from 2012 until 2026, after which it was acquired by the selling dealer.

Ballistic Missiles.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv kills one and injures 10, damaging medical facilities and student accommodation – photos
points: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv in the evening damaged medical facilities in the Dniprovskyi district and student accommodation in the Desnianskyi district.
Details: At 21:41, the Air Force warned of a ballistic missile threat from the Russian city of Bryansk.
Update: Klitschko later reported that a medical facility in the Dniprovskyi district had been damaged in the attack.

Ballistic Missiles.title: Paramedics caught under fire as Russian ballistic missiles slam Kyiv
points: Russia launched two waves of ballistic missiles at the capital overnight, targeting a major bridge, metro stations, and other civilian infrastructure.
Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a deadly attack overnight on Oct. 26-27, striking a university campus, a major bridge, an administrative building, and medical facilities.
Kyiv, a city of three million people, has been relentlessly assaulted by Russian ballistic missiles in recent months as Moscow exploits Ukraine's air defense shortage.

Ballistic Missiles.title: Pakistan’s Upgraded Fatah IV meets India’s 800km BrahMos Missile, Is Mumbai in Range?
points: The upgraded Fatah-IV missile test reshapes strategic calculations between Islamabad and New Delhi.

The country tested extended-range version of Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile, showing range exceeding 750 kms and potentially expanding Pakistan’s ability to threaten military installations deep inside Indian territory.

Although the missile’s maximum operational range has not been independently established, some assessments based on available imagery suggest that the upgraded version could eventually approach 1,000 kilometers.

Drones & Loitering Munitions.title: Centre clears Rs 2.12L-crore procurement proposals
points: The DAC also cleared the acquisition of other unmanned aerial system, surveillance aerial vehicles, integrated surveillance and strike system and long-range Kamikaze drone system for the Army.
Comment X Centre clears Rs 2.12L-crore procurement proposals.

The proposals were approved by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), the Defence Ministry’s highest decision-making body for military procurement, at a meeting chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

Drones & Loitering Munitions.title: From Kamikaze drones to new helicopters: What Indian Army, IAF and Navy will receive under DAC's Rs 2.12 lakh crore defence push | Full list
points: The DAC on Monday approved capital acquisition worth Rs 2.12 lak crore for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.

The approvals, granted through Acceptance of Necessity (AoN), cover a wide range of military equipment, including artillery systems, helicopters, air defence systems, surveillance platforms and drones.
The Defence Minister said around 82% of the total procurement will be sourced from Indian industry, supporting domestic defence manufacturing.

Drones & Loitering Munitions.title: Kamikaze drones, more K9 Vajras: Centre okays arms buys worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore
points: Self-propelled K9 Vajra guns, loitering munitions and helicopters cleared; Navy gets decoy system and 'major platforms.’

Copied NEW DELHI: The Union government on Monday gave the initial go-ahead to military procurement proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore, with more K9 Vajra self-propelled guns, kamikaze drones and counter-drone systems for the Army among the key approvals.

These include long-range unmanned aerial systems, surveillance UAVs, an integrated surveillance and strike system and a long-range kamikaze drone system, which the ministry said "will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army".
